title: CPT–APE terminology review index
count_note: The draft refers to a 25-rule watchlist, but the printed list includes 27 term groups; no two are silently discarded.
founder_correction: 2026-10-17: Gentiles/ethnos = nations or peoples lexically. The October 16 draft itself recognizes Israel can be among nations. Explicit founder clarification: not every occurrence called Gentiles denotes non-Israelites; other passages plainly contrast nations with Israel. Use the lexical starting sense with contextual referent analysis and no unreviewed mass text substitution.

terms.review: Check actual assembly referent instead of assuming institution.
Confirm function as royal or other anointed title in context.
Distinguish immersion terminology from ritual assumptions.

terms.proposal: nation(s) / people(s), honoring singular/plural grammar and immediate context
terms.review: FOUNDER CLARIFICATION: Greek ethnos denotes nation/people; ethnē denotes nations/peoples. Israel itself can be called a nation (Luke 7:5). Acts 4:27 contrasts nations with the people of Israel, so non-Israelite groups are meant there. Use nations/peoples as the lexical starting point, not as proof of outsider identity. Determine the actual referent for each verse by its context; never blanket-classify every Gentile as non-Israelite, and never perform an unreviewed global text replacement.
Tribal, regional and ethnic meanings must be evaluated in historical context; not automatically interchangeable.
Check whether the source actually has the Tetragrammaton; do not insert it without textual evidence.
Different senses depend on source, syntax, speaker and textual context.
Examine distinct source terms, context and imagery.

terms.proposal: age-related, enduring or everlasting as context warrants
terms.review: Duration must be evaluated contextually; the draft's automatic age-limited reading is not ratified.
Review Isaiah 14:4–12 and ancient-language evidence before approving a rendering.
Review Greek pascha at Acts 12:4 and context, rather than relying on English feast naming.
Review function, usage and audience; avoid assuming a later institutional rank.

terms.proposal: elder or priest according to source term
terms.review: Do not conflate presbyteros with hiereus / Hebrew kohen.
Assess commission, office and traditional equivalent, as context requires.
Determine grammatical role and audience; avoid later canonization assumptions.
Identify announcement and its topic; draft still needs approval.
Study change of mind, return and national or personal context.
Distinguish belief, loyalty and fidelity in immediate context.
Assess idiom and usage; no automatic replacement.
Check term and context; avoid unwarranted philosophical inference.
Distinguish physical wind, breath, disposition and divine Spirit.
Identify action, recipient and whether an honorific sense is intended.
Use underlying original term; do not pre-delete an English category.
Separate ancient covenant usage from modern edition section headings.
Identify source term; draft language is not a global correction.
Do not project later institutional distinction backwards without source evidence.

terms.proposal: accuser / slanderer / hostile spirit, context dependent
terms.review: Different Greek terms require separate analysis; no blanket substitution.
